description: A new type of search system with pattern recognition. Enterprise-grade search in a class library.
releaseNotes:
Release candidate. Four fixes to field roles and facets, three of them found in customer data, and
      two changes that can make working code throw or stop: two roles are refused on a field with no
      type, and a change that only a load can apply now returns the engine to Created. Nothing stored
      needs converting.
      
      - Fixed: a field given its first role on a loaded engine now takes effect when you call `Index()`,
        and `RequiresReindex` reports that the change needs one. This is the known limitation listed
        under RC210926. A field that was not Searchable, Filterable, Facetable or Sortable when the data
        was loaded holds no values for that field, so setting the flag produced no facets, no filter
        matches and no sorting, with nothing thrown. Documents that came into use since the last load are
        now read from their own JSON during `Index()`. A role added to a field that already had one is
        still a query-time change and still needs no reindex.
      - Fixed: `Facetable` set on a running engine is now seen by facet counting. The list of facetable
        fields was cached on first use and cleared only on disposal, and the results of an empty faceted
        search were cached separately, so a facet panel could keep answering with the old set of fields.
        Both are cleared when a field configuration is applied.
      - Fixed: a field that holds an array in some documents and a single value in others no longer
        loses either shape. The shape was taken from the first document carrying the field, and values of
        the other shape were stored under a name nothing reads, so they were missing from filters, facets
        and search without a word about it. Found in a customer export where 281 of 16,761 documents
        carried a bare string: a filter returned 15,521 documents where the answer was 15,733. Which side
        lost depended on document order, so the same data in a different order could have hidden most of
        the corpus. `Field.IsArray` is now true when any document shows an array, and never goes back.
      - Fixed: a facet on an array field counts a document once when its array repeats a value, so a
        facet count matches what a filter on that value returns. Measured on the same export, a facet said
        16,566 where the filter returned 15,733, because 850 documents carried the value twice.
      - Note: a facet keys on the value as stored, so a corpus that spells a value both ways lists it
        twice, and either entry filters to the documents of both spellings unless the filter is built
        case-sensitive. A facet count and a filter count therefore agree only for a filter created with
        `isCaseSensitive` true, which gives up the per-field posting index and loads by scanning: same
        answers, more work. Folding facet values to lower case was tried during this release and taken
        out again, because it changes what a user interface displays for every facet and only moves the
        disagreement to filters built the other way. `CreateValueFilter` now says this where you meet it.
      - Changed: setting `Filterable` or `Sortable` on a field with no type throws `ArgumentException`.
        A field that was null in every analyzed document has no type, a filter or a sort on it cannot
        work, and a filter cannot be repaired at the point of use because it is referenced by its
        serialized key and can sit inside a combined expression. Clearing either role is always allowed,
        which is how an older configuration is repaired. `Searchable` and `Facetable` do not read the type
        and are unaffected: setting `Searchable` on such a field prepares it, so a record inserted later
        that does carry a value is indexed and found.
      - Changed: `SetFieldConfiguration` returns the engine to Created when the change is one only a load
        can apply, so searches fail with a reason instead of answering as though the field had no values.
        The six are `Searchable`, `WordIndexing`, `Embeddable`, `PreloadFilters`, `BM25k1` and
        `HighResolution`. The change itself is kept, and the way on is a fresh `Load`, or
        `CreateInMemoryClone` with the change as field overrides, which applies it before the clone loads.
      - Added: `DocumentFields.RequiresReload(FieldProxy[])`, beside `RequiresReindex`, so you can ask
        which of the three a change needs before applying it: nothing, an `Index()`, or a load.
title: IndxSearchLib
